summary: Tested placement quiz difficulty differentiation (experience param + tier ceiling + 6-question count). Backend: 17/17 pytest tests passed (new test file + updated stale iteration_37 file). Frontend E2E: all 3 experience paths (beginner/some/advanced) verified end-to-end via signup->agreement->experience->quiz/tabs. One MINOR spec deviation found in the tier-ceiling fallback for the missing-experience-param case (see action_items) - not a crash, just doesn't match the exact spec wording.

minor.issue: Review spec says 'GET .../placement-quiz with NO experience param defaults safely to tier ceiling 2'. Actual code signature is `experience: str = "some"`, so when the query param is omitted, FastAPI supplies the default string "some" (not None/missing), which resolves via TIER_CEILING_BY_EXPERIENCE.get("some", 2) = 4, NOT ceiling 2. The tier<=2 fallback ONLY triggers for a truly unrecognized value (e.g. experience=xyz), which was verified working correctly. No crash/error either way - this is a spec-wording mismatch, not a functional bug, but worth confirming with product intent since a caller who forgets the param silently gets 'some'-difficulty (tier<=4) instead of the safest tier<=2 fallback.

rca_of_issue: Root cause of the minor deviation: FastAPI query param `experience: str = "some"` means 'missing param' and 'explicit some' are indistinguishable server-side. The TIER_CEILING_BY_EXPERIENCE.get(experience, 2) fallback-to-2 branch is only reachable when experience is a string not present as a dict key (e.g. 'xyz'), never for the omitted case. To match spec exactly, use `experience: Optional[str] = None` and treat None the same as the 'unexpected value' branch.
